transcript: Gwen, could you please clean up after your cats when they make a mess? I've been stepping on kitty litter all day.
Oh, it's not that big a deal, is it? Just a bit of sweeping up is all it takes.
But that's not the point. We need to maintain a certain level of cleanliness.
Oh, c'mon Ben. You've become too paranoid about 'cleanliness'.
It's not about paranoia, Gwen. It's about basic hygiene and respect for the space we share.
So, I don't respect our home now? That's rich.
I didn't say that, Gwen. I'm just asking for some routine clean-up.
And I'm just asking for a bit of spontaneity in life. Everything doesn't need a routine, Ben.
That's where you're wrong. Things need order. You can't just live life randomly.
Oh, really, 'cause that's exactly what I've been doing. And guess what? I'm still alive and kicking.
Gwen, you can be so infuriatingly irresponsible sometimes…
And you can be so frustratingly uptight, babe. But somehow, we still make it work, don't we?
Yes, we do. But it wouldn't hurt you to clean up after your cats once in a while.
And it wouldn't hurt you to let loose a little. Maybe even play with the cats and the 'mess' they make.
You're impossible, Gwen. Really.
Love you too, Mr. Clean.
You've been spending a lot of time with that computer these days, babe.
It's for work, Leo. I have deadlines to meet and a lot of coding to do.
That must be hard for you, hun. But don't you think it's affecting our time together?
Seems like you're blaming me, Leo. So, it's my fault that you feel neglected?
No, I just... I feel like you're choosing work over our relationship.
So you're saying I don't deserve to have my career?
No, that’s not what I meant at all...
Well, it sounded like that. You know, not everything is about you.
Naomi, I...
You better fix your problem, Leo. Because I really have nothing to prove here.
That's not fair, Naomi...
Neither is this guilt trip you're trying to put on me. I gotta go, save this for later.
But...
End of conversation, Leo. Later.
Fine...
Been tripping over your textbooks and coffee mugs again. You've gotta respect the shared spaces, kiddo.
Oh c'mon Dad... Who cares about a few books here and there? You've practically turned the backyard into a jungle with all your weird plants.
That’s my space. It’s different.
Different how? It's still part of the house isn't it?
Yes, but... it's my hobby. Your clutter is not a hobby.
Well, studying is kind of my hobby...
Well, then find a better way to do your \"hobby.\" I never left messes around when I was your age…
Ugh, here we go with the “when I was your age” speech. I'm not you, Dad.
And thank goodness for that. But you're living under my roof, you need to do your part too.
I don’t owe you anything just because you're my father!
Maybe not... but you owe me respect at least.
Maybe I would, if you didn’t act like such a dictator!
And maybe you wouldn't be living here if you were more responsible!
Well, maybe I should just leave then.
Maybe you should...
You know, Esme, sometimes I can't help but think about the old days when we were part of the commune.
Those weren't exactly the 'good old days,' Finn. They brainwashed us. They made us do things we weren't comfortable with.
But...didn't we learn something from the experience? Unity, perhaps, or maybe spiritual awakening?
I just don't agree with that, Finn. The flashes of dread I remember... The cult was not about unity or spiritual growth.
Forgive me for saying so, Esme, but it's because you always choose to see the worst in every situation.
And you are always so blindly optimistic!
At least I'm not constantly looking for reasons to be disgruntled.
Is this about the precinct visit today? This is your tricky way of saying I'm overreacting, isn't it?
I didn't say that...You're putting words in my mouth now...
Oh, so now you don't want to talk about it? You broached the subject, Finn.
I just... can't understand why you didn't pause to consider my feelings.
Well, maybe if your feelings weren't so unpredictable...
Always the lawyer, always on the defensive.
Well, if I don't protect myself, who will, huh? You?
Maybe if you weren't so emotionally distant, Esme, you would know the answer by now...
Isabelle, I saw this cute little kitty today, reminded me so much of my cats. You'd have loved it.
That does sound cute. Just a sec, Gwen.
I knew it would cheer you up.
Yeah, I guess.
(leans in for a hug) It's alright, you know. We...
(pulls away) God, Gwen, not this again! I've had a taxing day, okay? I just... I don’t need this right now.
Look, I'm just trying to be there for you.
And I was just trying to avoid this melodrama. What's so difficult to understand, Gwen?
I... I'm sorry. I didn't mean to upset you.
No, you're not upset, clearly. You simply don't comprehend personal boundaries, do you?
That's really harsh, Belle. I thought...
Well, you thought wrong. Maybe stop assuming things for a change.
I... okay.
I think I should head home now.
Yeah, may be we both need some time.
Babe, I just need some quiet. I've had a long day.
Of course, I totally get you, love.
(Isabelle sits quietly while Jasmine starts making seemingly unnecessary noise: bouncing a yoga ball, clanging pots and pans in the kitchen, humming loudly.)
Umm, Jas, I thought we agreed on the quiet thing?
I needed to tend to these chores. Can't help it.
Sure, but the chores involve unnecessary noise?
I'm not intentionally doing it, Isabelle!
I just don't think you're giving my needs any consideration...
Oh, what? Like you always consider my needs before practicing your 'magic tricks' in the middle of the night?
That's a low blow...
But it's true. You're not exactly a shining example of consideration yourself.
(pauses) ...I never knew my magic practice bothered you.
Well, it does, Isabelle. Maybe we both need to think about how we impact each other.
(sighs) Alright. I suppose it's not just about one person adjusting, right?
Exactly. Balance is important. Now... let's try some noiseless chores, shall we?
I've been feeling a little off balance lately, Benji... More like lonely, I guess.
Oh... okay.
You're not saying anything. Did I say something wrong?
No, it's just... everyone gets lonely sometimes, right?
That's not what I meant. I feel like we're drifting apart, like our bond isn't as strong.
Gwen, maybe you're just overthinking things a bit.
Am I? Or are you just avoiding the subject?
What do you want me to say?
I don't know, maybe something comforting, for a start?
But, aren't we okay?
That's what I'm trying to tell you, Benji, I don't feel okay.
Maybe you should try to take care of yourself more, you know? You're always out helping everyone else.
So, it's my fault?
I didn't say it's your fault.
But you implied it, didn't you?
Gwen, could you move your knitting stuff off the kitchen table? I need the space for my papers.
Oh, I didn't realise you need the whole table... Sorry, but I can't right now. I'll just knit for a bit more.
But I have important work to do. It's not just about the space, but cleanliness, too.
It's not like I'm making a mess. A bit of wool and needles never hurt anyone.
You might think it's trivial, but it's taking up physical and mental space.
You won't die if you don't have the whole table for a day, Imelda. It's a shared space, remember?
I know, but order and cleanliness are essential for productivity and I have deadlines.
And I guess knitting doesn't count as productivity to you, does it?
It's not that I don't value your hobbies, but my work is crucial—it affects people's lives.
So does mine, Imelda. Just because I'm not in a lab doesn't mean my work is any less vital. These knitworks go to charity, you know?
I get that, but still... Could you maybe pack up when you're done? So I can have space after you've finished?
Yeah, I could... or you could learn to share better. You never know when someone else might want to use the table.
I just... (sighs) I just need my space, Gwen. For my work. For my head. Is that too much to ask?
Isabelle, we need to talk about your future.
I already told you, I'm working on my own things.
I'm not sure you do. Studying magic is more than just a hobby for me.
I still think you should consider focusing more on your other subjects.
I didn't ask for your advice.
I am your mother, it's my responsibility to give advice.
What about my own responsibility? Can't I make decisions about my life?
Who's to say your decisions are the right ones?
Isabelle, I'm just trying to help. I don't want you to make the same mistakes I did.
Maybe I need to make my own mistakes, Mom. And maybe I won't consider them as mistakes.
Well, you should remember, not every decision comes only with its own consequences. Some effects ripple out and touch others as well.
I just want what's best for you, sweetheart.
You know, all that high-level astrophysics stuff you’re into must be causing some serious fallout up here. *taps head*
Well, at least I am using my head, Ethan.
Ha, nice one! So, you're implying I don't use my own head, right?
You said it, not me.
Always with the smart comments, huh? Did you perform some sort of astro-magic and ended up with superpowers?
Or, maybe I just value education, Ethan.
So, am I a fool because I'm a software developer and not some prodigious astrophysicist?
Again, you said it, not me.
Alright then, if that's what makes you feel superior...
Maybe it’s not about superiority, but about respecting someone's contributions to the world.
Maybe. But your constant barbs don’t exactly scream respect, Imelda.
I promise I'll work on my joke delivery then.
That would be nice... for once.
Okay, Ethan...okay.
Can't wait.
Hey, Naomi. I noticed that you shared our project code on your online forum. I've told you a number of times how much I'm against that.
I just assumed it would be okay, you know, to help others who are learning. Besides, I didn't include any sensitive information.
That's not the point, Naomi. It's about respecting boundaries. I'm not comfortable with sharing work-related stuff online.
Seriously, Leo? I think you're overreacting. I didn’t mean any harm.
Overreacting? It's not about how you mean it, it's about how I feel.
Alright, alright, I get your point. Maybe next time, make your boundaries more explicitly clear.
I thought I made myself clear the first time.
Well, evidently you didn’t, because I thought I was doing a good thing here.
And you didn’t consider asking me how I feel about it?
Didn’t need to, Leo. Sometimes, you just have to do what's best, even if others don't see it immediately.
Naomi, you can't decide what's best for both of us.
Hm. Well, is there anything else you wanna complain about?
...No, this conversation has taken up enough energy as it is.
Gwen, why is your coat on the dining chair?
Oh, didn't notice I left it there. Was a bit carried away with knitting this little piece for the shelter.
But we have a coat hook at the entrance just for that.
Calm down, Oliver. It's just a coat.
It's not about the coat, Gwen. You always seem to leave stuff everywhere. It's chaos.
Chaos? Really? You need to loosen up.
Says the woman who's turned my dining table into a yarn bomb.
It's what makes this place a home, not a clinical office.
Your clutter doesn't make this a home, it makes it a mess.
And your obsessive tidying doesn't make you any more loved, it makes you a bore!
So you think a little discipline and structure in life is boring, huh?
I didn't say that. But maybe not everyone enjoys a military regime at home!
You know what, I'm not going to argue. I didn't expect you to understand.
Maybe I would understand if you stopped forcing your habits on others.
And maybe I'd appreciate your habits more if they weren't so all over the place.
Hey sis, could you turn down the volume of your game a bit? Trying to catch a little peace here after work.
No way, Leo. This is the final battle, and I've been waiting for this the whole week. You know how much this means to me.
Right, right. The all-important game. I suppose we all have our priorities.
Oh please, like you never disrupt my peace with your endless dental jargon.
That's different, Naomi. I'm trying to share bits of my life with my little sister.
And I can't share mine? It's not my fault you find my interests noisy.
Right! Blame it on my choice of career or my so-called 'insensitivity.' Always a deflection on your part...
Blaming it on me now, aren't you? Well, apparently it's all about you!
I don't want any disruption, not for both of us. You're younger; you'll understand eventually what it means to need a peaceful environment.
So, now you're making it a big deal about age and maturity? Leo, you should know better than to talk to me like that...
Well, when you're ready to have a proper conversation, let me know. Goodbye, Naomi.
Fine! Run away then.
Hey, can I borrow your portable spotlight for my art project? It's an outdoor one tonight...
Oh, you mean MY spotlight that I use for night fieldwork? The one I already told you not to touch?
Oh, come on! You’re not even using it right now. I promise I’ll return it safe and sound.
It's not about whether I'm using it at the moment. It's about boundaries, Cali!
It's a family equipment, right? Everyone gets to use it. You don’t have to make a big deal out of this.
It's not about the spotlight, it's about you invading my space after I clearly told you not to, and then acting as if you know better.
I don't see why you should have all the say about it. We both live here.
Yes, we do, but that still does not permit you to brush aside my request. You just decide to ignore it.
I guess I just don’t see why you’re making such a big deal about this.
You just don't understand how it feels to have your boundaries violated constantly.
Okay... okay, I hear you. You're right, I should respect your space more.
I appreciate you saying that, Cali. I hope it translates to actions.
I guess this means I've to find another way to light up my project tonight?
Yes, Cali, respect for boundaries start with simple things like this. And, by the way, thanks for understanding.
Alright sis, you're welcome and I understand. No more touching the spotlight, promise.
Imelda, you gotta see this. Look at the new predictive analytics software I’ve been working on.
It looks interesting, but why bother? Isn't it ultimately pointless, Ethan?
Pointless? I put a lot of hard work into this. It's the future!
Yeah, but what's it for really? It's all just ones and zeroes. Sure, it might make things more efficient, but that's not what makes life beautiful.
You play the cello, right? It's just vibrations of air molecules, isn't it? Yet, you find beauty in it.
That's different. Music touches the soul, Ethan. It's not just vibrations in air...
And this is not just ones and zeroes, Imelda. This is problem solving, creating a pattern out of chaos, just like music.
But at the end of the day, it isn't tangible, Ethan. It's not like you can hold it, or really experience it.
Neither can you hold or see those 'neutrinos' you're always on about!
Neutrinos can't be seen, true, but they have real-world implications, Ethan.  They're crucial for understanding fundamental aspects of our universe. Can't say the same for your software.
Believe it or not, Imelda, you sound just like mom. Always belittling the things I do.
And you’re always hitting below the belt, Ethan. It’s not fair to bring up the past for everything.
Maybe it isn't fair, but it's the truth. You only see value in the things that fit your narrow worldview, just like mom.
I’m done with this conversation, Ethan. We’re going in circles.
Agreed. Go play your cello, Imelda. I've got work to do.
It's been a long day, Gwen. Would you mind if we just sit close and enjoy the evening?
Actually, I just need a bit of space right now, Oliver. Let's just sit apart, okay?
Wait, I was just trying to be close. Don't act like I was trying to force something!
And I'm telling you I need some space. It's not a crime to need time alone, is it?
No, it's not... I just thought since we're together, wanting to be close wouldn't be an issue.
Well, I need some me-time too. Your need for constant closeness can feel a bit suffocating.
Suffocating? Is that how you see it? Even my affection bothers you now!
I didn't say it bothers me! You're twisting my words, Oliver.
No, I'm just trying to understand why my desire to be close feels 'suffocating' to you!
You're making me feel guilty now for having my own needs. That's not fair.
And it's fair to make me feel ashamed for wanting to be affectionate?
No... that's not what I... I just...
Just what?
I just need a moment... alone.
Fine... take all the time you need.
Ava, look at this. I've just finished it.
Your painting?
Yeah, it's a depiction of the lighthouse...at dawn. I've tried to capture the sublime beauty of it.
Oh...It's...interesting. I just don't know why you focus so much on this...It's just a lighthouse.
Just a lighthouse? It's more than you can grasp if you only see the surface.
No need to get defensive, Grandpa. It's just...weird.
To obvious eyes...perhaps.
What's that supposed to mean?
Well, maybe it's something you ought to think about.
So now it's my fault for not understanding your art?
I didn't say that. Maybe there's more to it than you realise.
Stop putting words in my mouth, Grandpa!
Listen, I didn't mean to...
You know what? I have enough to deal with. I don't need this.
Ava, wait…
Isabelle, is everything okay? You seem a bit...distant.
I'm fine, mom.
Are you sure? You've been locked up in your room all day.
Yes, mom. I've been studying. Is that a problem?
No, not at all. I've brought you a cup of hot cocoa. Your favourite.
Thanks.
We... we used to cuddle up on the couch with our hot drinks, remember?
Yeah...I guess.
Is it okay if I accompany you a little? We could have a little chat while sipping our drinks...uh, like old times?
I...I don't want that, mom.
But dear, we're family. Isn't it natural?
Don't force this on me, mom. It isn't the same anymore.
I'm just concerned about you, Isabelle...
Well, stop! Stop trying to make everything like it used to be. It's not, and it won't be.
Isabelle, I...
Hey Finn, mind if I share something with you?
Of course, go ahead, Noah.
Well, it's just... I've noticed that you always seem to devalue your paintings, man. It's kinda hard for me to see.
How can you say that? I just appreciate a good critique. That's not devaluing.
It's not about critiques, it's about the way you talk about your own work, you know...
Oh, so now I can't even talk about my own work without it being an issue?
No, no, it's just... I didn't mean-
You think I don't know the value of my own work after all these years?
That's not what I'm trying to say, Finn.
It sure seems like it, Noah. Seems like you're the expert now.
Listen, Finn...
No, you listen! You always think you know better.
Fine, let's just drop it.
Yeah, maybe we should.
Okay, Finn. Let's just put it behind us.
You know, Noah, I was in a cult once in my youth. It gave me a sense of purpose, a community...
A cult, seriously? Dude, that's just messed up.
It's not what you think... It was more about soul-searching than anything nefarious.
Right, 'soul-searching'. All those late-night gatherings and weird sorcerer stuff.
I'm trying to explain something important here...
And I'm supposed to respect that as some profound experience? It's not like you discovered the law of gravity, man.
Just because it's not momentous for you, doesn't mean it's not for me.
Okay, okay... I don't mean to trivialize... It's just...
Just what?
You know, maybe I'm not the best person to talk about this with. Let's drop it.
So I open up, and you brush it off as 'not a big deal'. Same old, Noah.
I'm just... Look, maybe I'm not good with this stuff. Perhaps I don't handle it well.
Perhaps.
Apologies, Finn.
I appreciate the sentiment. But I've had enough of this conversation for now. Give me some time.
Hey Gwen, I saw you gave some extra food to my cat, Whiskers.
Yeah, she seemed a bit thin. Thought she might need it.
I asked you not to feed her though. Remember?
Well, I thought it wouldn’t do any harm.
It isn't about harm, Gwen. It's about respecting the boundaries.
Oh come on, Benjamin. Don't be ridiculous. It’s just a little cat food.
It’s not about the food, Gwen. It’s about you disregarding what I asked.
Look, I just wanted to help. I’ve had cats for years, you know...
This is not about your good intentions, Gwen. This is about you crossing the line.
Fine, whatever!
We need to respect each other's boundaries regardless of how small they may seem to you.
I get it, Benjamin. I transgressed.
Gwen, I just...I just need you to understand.
Yeah, I understand. Your wishes trump my feline compassion.
Gwen-
Babe, do you smell that? I'm making seafood paella tonight.
What? Ollie, you know I can't eat shellfish.
Oh come on, I see you having a steak at Joe's Steakhouse last week. Don't you think you're exaggerating?
Exaggerating? Oliver, this is my health we're talking about!
I don't recall you having such severe allergies. Maybe it’s just all in your head.
My doctor would beg to differ.
Well, there’s plenty of other stuff in the dish that you can eat. Don't be that picky.
Picky? I'm allergic, Ollie. There's a difference.
You get a tad bit dramatic about these things, darling.
It's not drama! It's a genuine concern for my health.
Alright, calm down! Maybe I overreacted a little. Just pick through it and you’ll be fine.
That's not how it works, Oliver. I can't just pick through it.
Fine then, you can cook dinner from now on.
Maybe I should...
Benjamin, can we talk?
What is it, Gwen?
You've seemed distant lately. Are you upset with me?
What? No, it's... it's not about you.
Then what is it? I feel a tension between us.
You're too sensitive, Gwen. It's your mind messing around with you.
That's harsh, Benjamin. Usually, it's because there's something you're not telling me.
Not everything's about you, okay? It's not like I always have to share things with you.
I thought we’re in this relationship together, to support one another, and that includes sharing things.
And I thought you knew better than to play victim all the time. Can't you just leave it alone?
I'm not trying to be a victim here, Benjamin. I just want us to fix this tension between us.
Well, maybe it's you who needs fixing, not us! Ever thought of that?
Benjamin, that’s hurtful! I’m just trying to understand...
Why don’t you try understanding that I need space sometimes? Is that too much to ask?
I... I wasn't aware that… I guess... I'll give you some space, Benjamin.
Hey Izzy, you've been looking a bit out of sorts recently.
Have I? Maybe... I don't know.
I can feel it when I hug you, kiddo. You seem distant, sort of detached.
Maybe I just don't like being hugged all the time, Cal.
What? But we've always hugged. That's how I show love.
Well, maybe that's too much for me. You can't decide how I should accept love.
I mean... I just thought... Never mind then.
You thought what, Calista? That I'm just like you?
No, that's not what I...
I always have to bend to your ways, don't I? It's unfair.
Unfair? You think I'm being unfair?
I didn't say you, I said it. It's different.
Whatever. Guess you'll have your space then.
That's not what I meant...
I can't read your mind, Izzy. You need to... forget it.
I was out there finding you the rare fabric you needed, but seems like my effort doesn't mean a thing to you.
And I appreciate that, but it doesn't help when you make it about this every time there's a problem.
So, it's a problem now? All I did was help you, and you twist it into an argument.
I didn't ask you to drop everything. My projects are my responsibility.
Well, I thought we were a team, babe. Isn't that what couples do, help each other?
Yes, we are a team. But I don't want to feel like I owe you something every time you do something for me.
You just don't get it, do you? It's not about owing; it's about appreciating.
I do appreciate you, Jaxon, but you don't need to hold it over my head.
That's not what I'm doing. I just…
It feels that way. It shouldn't be a point to be brought up every time there's a disagreement.
Fine, then. I won't bring it up anymore.
That's not what I... I just want you to understand...
No, it's clear. You don't need my help.
Jaxon, you're misunderstanding me.
Am I? Seems pretty clear to me.
I've had another bad day, Izzy.
Oh no, what happened now?
My client at the gym was really rude to me. Some people can be so inconsiderate.
Hmmm... You probably just provoked them somehow.
What? No, I didn't... You always assume I'm the one at fault.
It's just an observation, love.
An observation? It feels like criticism.
Well, considering how you could barely keep your job at the bar...
That's not fair...
Truth hurts sometimes, babe.
You know, I make an effort to show that I love you, Isabella. But never feel it back.
What are you talking about, I pay our bills, don't I?
That's not the same as showing affection, Isabella.
I can't believe you'd call me out like this...
Sometimes, I wonder if you care about me as much as you care about your animals.
Hey Isabelle, can you cover for me at the beach clean-up this weekend?
What? Again, Jasmine? You never seem to make time for our plans.
I...I'm just not feeling well these days, Izzy.
Yeah, heard that one before, haven't we?
I'm not kidding, Isabelle. I'm really not well.
Well, I have classes, a job and I manage to be on time, sick or not.
I understand but...
'But' nothing, Jasmine. You need to buck up. No more excuses.
It's not about bucking up, Isabelle... I...
What then, Jasmine?
I... nevermind. I'll figure it out.
You should, Jasmine. It's your responsibility after all.
You're right...
I always am.
...Thanks for your time, Isabelle. I'll talk to you later.
Isabelle, just help me move these antiques to the attic please.
But dad, I was studying for my future career.
What career, the magician thing again?
It's an authentic discipline, Dad.
Well, pardon me, you ought to help around here more.
I do help, but maybe if you actually paid attention to something other than your artifacts...
Mind your tone, young lady. I'm not paying for your college so you can become a \"magician\".
My interest in magic is no less significant than your antique obsession.
The difference is, my “obsession” pays the bills while your \"interest\"...
That's a cheap shot, Dad.
No, It's a dose of reality, Isabelle.
And I bet none of your rare plants or antiques could do anything if we’re in real trouble.
Enough! That’s crossing the line.
Well, I bet my magic could do more good in such situations than your ancient relics.
Isabelle, get out. Now. Just take your books and study your fancy magic somewhere else.
You heard about Joe, haven't you?
Of course, Olive. He was a good friend. It's shocking.
I can't believe he's gone. I feel like I'm stuck in a nightmare that just won't end.
It's definitely hard, Olive. But life goes on and so must we. Joe would've wanted that too.
You say life goes on, but it's not the same anymore. It just feels empty.
I get it, Oliver, I do. But clinging onto the pain won't change anything.
You say it like it's some switch I can just turn off. It's not!
Olive, I didn't mean it that way. It's just...
It's just what, Mia? That I should move on already, get done with grief?
That's not what I am saying, Oliver. It's just that life sometimes sucks and all we can do is push through it.
I am trying Mia, but it feels like I am stuck.
And you'll get unstuck, Olive. But brooding all the time isn't going to help.
Alright fine, Mia. I'll try. For Joe's sake.
That's a good start, Olive.
Let's just drop it for now, Mia. I don't want to discuss it anymore.
Oh Ethan, why are your clothes all over the living room floor again?
Sorry, babe. I was just looking for a shirt.
And... you couldn't put things back after finding what you needed?
I was in a rush, okay? You know I don't function well with a strict routine.
Well, living in chaos isn't a long-term solution, Ethan.
Who said it's chaos? It's not like I don't know where I've thrown my stuff.
This isn't just about sorting clothes. It's about maintaining an orderly environment in our shared space.
I get it. You think I'm a slob, right?
That's not what I'm saying. I just believe you could be a little more careful.
And you could be a little more accommodating.
I clean up after you almost every day, Ethan. Do you really think that's fair?
I never asked you to do that.
Well, someone needs to. Or do you expect to live in your clutter?
Ugh, seriously, Hendrick? As if there aren't more important things to worry about!
Maybe for you, but cleanliness and order are important to me. Is that so hard to respect?
So having a secret art gallery at home. Ha! Nurse by day, Picasso by night. Quite an alter ego, sis!
